Bakhmaro

A mountain resort of wooden chalets at 1,950 m where sea and alpine air meet — open only in summer.

Time needed
6 h
From Tbilisi
355 km · 6:30
Road
Unpaved sections
Car needed
Off-road 4x4
Season
June–September
Entry
free

Bakhmaro is a climatic resort in the mountains of Guria, at roughly 1,950 metres. Its unusual reputation rests on the air: the Black Sea is only a few dozen kilometres away, yet the resort sits high in the alpine zone, so humid marine air mixes with dry mountain air. From the Soviet period onward people with respiratory problems were sent here to recover, and that tradition still shapes who comes.

The architecture is unlike anywhere else in Georgia. This is not a town of hotels but a scattered settlement of wooden cottages, many raised on stilts, spread across open pasture. In winter Bakhmaro is effectively empty: snow lies metres deep and the road closes. Life starts in July and finishes in early September.

Things to know:

  • The season is short — realistically July and August, with late June and early September marginal
  • The road is rough — the last few dozen kilometres are unsurfaced and get worse after rain
  • Services are basic — a few cafes, family guesthouses, no ATM

In August the settlement hosts a traditional horse race, one of the best-known events in the region, which fills the place completely for several days. Outside that week, the appeal is quiet: meadows, mist rolling in from the sea below, and long evenings.

Practical advice

Plan a visit only in summer, and book accommodation in advance — in August, especially during the race week, there is essentially nothing free. Nights at 1,950 metres are cold even in midsummer, so warm clothing is genuinely necessary. There is no ATM and no pharmacy: bring cash and any medication you need. The last fuel is in Chokhatauri or Ozurgeti. Mobile coverage is patchy, so download the route for offline use before you leave the main road.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Bakhmaro is about 355 km and six and a half hours from Tbilisi. Take the E60 west through Khashuri, the Rikoti section, Kutaisi and Samtredia, then turn off toward Chokhatauri. The serious part begins there: roughly 50 km of mountain dirt road, steep, narrow and heavily potholed, which takes two to three hours on its own. A sedan is not an option here — a high-clearance 4x4 is required, and even then the surface demands patience. Do not set out on a rainy day, as sections turn to deep mud quickly.
